payout_quote: The winning designer receives the prize money, and the client gets the design files, and full copyright to the winning design.
steps: Create a free 99designs designer account and build your portfolio profile.
Browse open contest listings in the 99designs marketplace.
Read a contest brief and submit original designs before the deadline (contests run about seven days; fast-track 1/2/3-day options exist).
Incorporate client feedback through the competition rounds.
If the client selects your design as the winner, you receive the prize money.
catches: Spec work: only the winning designer is paid — contests average around 110 entries, so most entrants earn nothing for their time.
The prize amount is set by the client per contest; there is no fixed payout.
Non-guaranteed contests may award no prize at all; prefer contests marked guaranteed.
Time spent on losing entries is unpaid — that is the core cost of this channel.
You need a competitive portfolio to win against experienced designers.
biggest_catch: Only the winner gets paid: with ~110 entries per contest on average, the expected payout for any single entry is near zero, and losing work is entirely unpaid.
eligibility: Free 99designs designer account; must be able to deliver original design work and receive payouts via supported methods.
timing: Contests run about 7 days (fast-track 1-3 days); prize paid after winner selection and file handover.

c1.evidence: 99designs' own help center (support.99designs.com) defines the mechanism: 'A design contest is a competition between designers to create the winning design for a client's design brief' and 'The winning designer receives the prize money'.

c2.evidence: Official terms state the prize is set per contest by the client; no fixed designer payout range is published — framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official contest flow: brief, package, contest stages over seven days, winner picked, prize paid.

c4.evidence: Entering contests is free for designers; no entry fee documented.

s1.note: Eligibility is a free designer account; effectively gated by design skill/portfolio.

s2.note: Framed as variable, winner-takes-most spec work; no fixed amount promised.
